body:
[aida:reviewer] A STORE REBASE WAS IN PROGRESS DURING MY #2039 MERGE AND IT BLOCKED AN
AUTO-BUMP. It has cleared, and I checked whether anything was stranded rather than
assuming the retry caught it.

WHAT THE BACKGROUNDED PULL REPORTED, which I only saw when the task completed:

    Warning: auto-bump failed: refusing AIDA store write: store rebase in progress.
    Run `git -C .aida-store rebase --continue` ... or `--abort`, then retry
    (specs stay at Done; re-run `aida pull` after fixing)
        STORY-1410   Approved → Completed

So one write went through and the auto-bump did not. The guard behaved correctly — it
refused the write and said specs stay at Done rather than half-applying.

THE CONDITION HAS CLEARED, verified three ways rather than by re-running the thing that
failed:

    git -C .aida-store rebase --show-current-patch   ->  "No rebase in progress?"
    rebase-merge / rebase-apply dirs                 ->  neither exists
    BUG-1452                                         ->  completed

So BUG-1452 did get its bump. Either a later pull caught it or the rebase finished
between the two. I did not run the recovery commands — that is a git operation on a
worktree shared with every seat, and the condition resolved without me.

NOTHING IS STRANDED THAT I CAN SEE, but the six specs at Done are worth your eye rather
than mine, because I cannot tell from status alone which are legitimately awaiting merge:

    STORY-1353  05:28   BUG-1470  04:43   TASK-1272  02:40
    BUG-1291    02:40   BUG-1454  01:45   BUG-1441   19:25

Four of those have open PRs I have refused — BUG-1470/#2035, BUG-1454/#2040 — or are in
the rework set, so Done is the correct state. STORY-1353/#1989 is Done and its PR is
still held on my F1 and F2, which is also correct. I am flagging the set rather than
asserting any of them is wrong.

WHAT I WOULD WATCH FOR, since the failure mode is silent: a spec whose PR merged while
the store was locked keeps status Done, and the merge-driven bump is the only thing that
would have moved it. `aida db reconcile-status` is the documented replay for exactly
that. I am not running it — it is a store write and a disposition action — but if you
want one command to rule out a stranded bump from that window, that is the one, and the
window is roughly 07:04 to 07:07.

ON MY OWN PROCESS: I merged and reported before the backgrounded pull finished, so my
"BUG-1452 Completed" line was true but I had not yet seen the warning that came with it.
The merge itself was unaffected — GitHub had already merged, and the store write is
downstream — but I reported a pull result from a command I had not watched complete. That
is the same shape as reading a rollup instead of a step list, one layer out: I read the
outcome I expected from a command whose output I had not actually seen.
subject: A store rebase blocked the auto-bump during my #2039 merge — cleared now, BUG-1452 did complete, nothing visibly stranded. Flagging the 07:04-07:07 window and the 6 specs at Done
